title: Humoral and cellular function of B cells in malignant transition and response to immunotherapy of breast cancer
summary:
This study looks at B lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell in our immune system and how these cells behave during different stages of breast cancer. While it is well described that B cells are found near tumors and are linked to better survival rates, researchers don't fully understand their role in helping cancer grow or how they influence a patient's response to immunotherapy.
The research project will examine a total of 120 patients at three different stages of breast cancer: Ductal carcinoma in situ, a very early, non-invasive stage, early breast cancer that hasn't spread to distant organs and finally, metastatic breast cancer, defined by a stage when breast cancer spread to other parts of the body.
By looking at both "responders" (people who do well with treatment) and "non-responders," the project aims to see how B cells change and organize themselves into clusters near the tumor and if the presence and arrangement of these cells can predict who will benefit from immunotherapy (treatments that help the immune system fight cancer). As a perspective, understanding the "patterns" of these immune cells could lead to new ways to treat breast cancer more effectively by specifically targeting B cell activity.

interventions.name: Retrospective study of humoral and cellular B-cell immune responses in patients of the investigators own institution diagnosed with DCIS (n=40) or early breast cancer (n=40) between 2010 and 2020, and in patients diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer (n=40) between 2020 and 2025. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Completeness of EMR/KIS records for clinic-pathologic and demographic data
•	Availability of treatment naïve, representative core needle biopsy or surgically resected tissue; sTILs ≥ 10% (ITWG)
•	DCIS: Histologically confirmed diagnosis of DCIS (pTis pN0 cM0), 
•	EBC: Histologically confirmed diagnosis of invasive breast cancer of no special type (NST)
•	MBC: Histologically confirmed diagnosis of inoperable, locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer of no special type (NST), treatment with ICB (Atezolizumab or Pembrolizumab) according to standard of care. Monotherapy OR combination with chemotherapy OR combination with targeted therapy.
•	Complete follow up of ≥ 5 years, in line with standard of care guidelines
•	Known ER, PR, HER2 Status
Exclusion criteria:
•	Any other history of neoplasms
•	Inflammatory breast cancer
•	Metaplastic breast cancer
•	Known current or past treatment with systemic immunostimulatory agents (including but not limited to interferons or interleukin [IL] −2) 
•	Known history of autoimmune disease prior to the diagnosis of breast cancer, including but not limited to myasthenia gravis, myositis, autoimmune hepatitis, systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, vascular thrombosis associated with antiphospholipid syndrome, Wegener’s granulomatosis, Sjögren’s syndrome, Guillain-Barré syndrome, multiple sclerosis, vasculitis, or glomerulonephritis. 
(Patients with autoimmune-related hypothyroidism are permitted)
•	History of HIV infection
•	History of tuberculosis
•	History diagnosis of invasive breast associated with pregnancy or puerperium
